questions.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)=⟨\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,t⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡(3t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(3t))+1} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\sqrt{(9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)^{2}+(-9\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\sqrt{{9}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡3t+{cos}^{2}⁡3t)} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\,\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}\,}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{9}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})⟩,\,0\le s<10\pi .
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}))⟩ \\  & =⟨-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})\cdot \frac{1}{5},\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})\cdot \frac{1}{5}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})\cdot \frac{1}{5},\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})\cdot \frac{1}{5}⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-\frac{1}{5}|\sqrt{{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${T}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+4{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2 \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))^{2}+(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)+16{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡(2t)+{cos}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\,2\,}{4}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\frac{\sqrt{5}s}{3}⟩,\,0\le s\le 4\pi .
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{5}s}{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-\frac{1}{3}|\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{2})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{2})+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
